Core concepts

Request & Response

Every field and helper on the wrapped req and res objects, from req.accepts() to res.format() and res.sendFile().

The wrappers#

Each request is wrapped once. Node's IncomingMessage becomes a Request and its ServerResponse becomes a Response. Both originals stay reachable, so the wrapper is a convenience layer rather than a cage:

js
req.raw;   // the IncomingMessage
res.raw;   // the ServerResponse

Anything the wrapper does not cover (req.raw.setTimeout(), res.raw.writeHead(), res.raw.socket) is one property away. Everything the wrapper does cover is listed below.

Request#

Request parses the URL, query string, cookies and client IP in its constructor, so per-request work happens once, not on every property read.

MemberTypeNotes
rawIncomingMessageThe underlying stream
appAppThe app handling this request
methodstring'GET', 'POST', …
urlstringCurrent URL, minus any stripped mount prefix
originalUrlstringThe original URL, unchanged
pathstringPathname only, no query string
searchstringQuery string including ?, or ''
queryobjectParsed query; repeated keys become arrays
paramsobjectRoute parameters, set during dispatch
bodyanySet by body-parser middleware
cookiesobjectParsed Cookie header, j: values decoded
headersobjectLower-cased header map
hostnamestringHost without the port
protocol`'http' \'https'`
securebooleanX-Forwarded-Proto or a TLS socket
ipstringClient IP, honouring trust proxy
ipsstring[]Forwarded chain, nearest first
js
app.get('/search', (req, res) => {
  res.json({
    path: req.path,                 // '/search'
    q: req.query.q,                 // 'cats'
    tags: req.query.tag,            // ['a', 'b'] for ?tag=a&tag=b
    ip: req.ip,
  });
});

Request methods#

MethodReturns
req.header(name)The header value (case-insensitive) or undefined
req.get(name)Alias for header()
req.accepts(...types)The first accepted type, or false
req.is(...types)Whether the request Content-Type matches
js
req.header('user-agent');
req.accepts('json', 'html');   // 'json' | 'html' | false
req.is('json');                // true for application/json
req.is('json', 'text/*');      // true for JSON or any text type

accepts() with no arguments returns the raw Accept header (defaulting to */*). is() accepts shorthand names ('json', 'html') and media ranges such as 'text/*'.

Cookies#

The Cookie header is parsed for you. Values written as j: JSON — which is what res.cookie() produces for object values — are decoded back:

js
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  const theme = req.cookies.theme;         // string
  const prefs = req.cookies.prefs;         // object, if written as j: JSON
  res.json({ theme, prefs });
});

Response#

Response makes every mutator return this, so calls chain:

js
res.status(201).type('json').send({ ok: true });
MemberDescription
res.rawThe underlying ServerResponse
res.reqThe matching Request
res.localsA per-response object for your own data
res.statusCodeGet/set the status code
res.headersSenttrue once the response has started
res.finishedtrue once the response has ended

Setting headers#

js
res.status(200);
res.set('X-Request-Id', 'abc');           // one header
res.set({ 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' }); // many at once
res.header('X-Other', 'v');               // alias for set()
res.append('Set-Cookie', 'a=1');          // append to a multi-value header
res.get('Content-Type');                  // read one back
res.vary('Accept');                       // add to Vary, de-duplicated

vary() merges with any existing Vary value and ignores duplicates.

Content type#

js
res.type('json');     // application/json; charset=utf-8
res.type('html');     // text/html; charset=utf-8
res.type('.css');     // text/css; charset=utf-8
res.type('image/png'); // used verbatim when it contains "/"

Sending a body#

res.send() picks a behaviour from the value it is given:

BodyContent-TypeBehaviour
null / undefinedtext/plainEmpty body, Content-Length: 0
Bufferapplication/octet-streamRaw bytes
object / arrayapplication/jsonDelegates to res.json()
string / numbertext/htmlWritten as UTF-8

A Content-Type is only set when the response does not already have one. res.json(value) sets application/json; charset=utf-8 when needed and serializes with JSON.stringify.

js
res.json({ ok: true });
res.send('<h1>Hello</h1>');
res.send(Buffer.from('bytes'));
res.sendStatus(204);          // status + reason phrase as text

The write-once guard#

res.send(), res.json() and friends check headersSent || writableEnded first. A stray second res.json() is silently ignored instead of crashing with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT:

js
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ first: true });
  res.json({ second: true });   // no-op
});

Cookies#

js
res.cookie('session', 'abc123', {
  httpOnly: true,
  secure: true,
  sameSite: 'lax',
  maxAge: 1000 * 60 * 60,   // milliseconds
  path: '/',
});

res.clearCookie('session');   // expires it immediately

res.cookie() merges into any existing Set-Cookie header rather than overwriting it, so several cookies can be set in one response. Supported options: path, maxAge (ms), expires, domain, secure, httpOnly, sameSite (true means Strict) and partitioned. Object values are stored as j: JSON, which req.cookies decodes automatically.

Redirects and downloads#

js
res.redirect('/login');          // 302
res.redirect(301, '/new');       // explicit status
res.sendStatus(403);             // 403 with the reason phrase as body

res.attachment('report.csv');    // Content-Disposition: attachment
res.sendFile('reports/q3.pdf');  // resolves a path from the cwd
res.download('reports/q3.pdf', 'Q3 2026.pdf');

redirect() accepts both (url, status) and (status, url). sendFile() and download() share the static-file engine — see Static files for conditional and range requests.

Content negotiation#

res.format() chooses a handler from the client's Accept header, sets Vary: Accept, and falls back to default or 406:

js
app.get('/greet', (req, res) => {
  res.format({
    json: () => res.json({ hello: 'world' }),
    html: () => res.send('<h1>Hello</h1>'),
    default: () => res.status(406).send('Not Acceptable'),
  });
});

Keys may be shorthands (json, html) or full media types. Evaluation uses the same req.accepts() logic as Request.

Low-level writes#

When you need the socket directly:

js
res.write('chunk');
res.end();
res.raw.end(compressedBuffer);

res.write() and res.end() return the underlying write result / this respectively. Prefer res.send() unless you are streaming or compressing manually.

A worked example#

js
import { createApp, json } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();
app.use(json());

app.post('/users', (req, res) => {
  const wantsHtml = req.accepts('html') === 'html';

  res.status(201).set('X-Created', 'yes');
  res.cookie('lastUser', { id: 7 }, { httpOnly: true });

  if (wantsHtml) {
    res.type('html').send('<p>Created</p>');
  } else {
    res.json({ created: req.body, id: 7 });
  }
});

app.listen(3000);
